items.title: Johari: Cheaper EVs must come with wider charging network
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The development of public charging infrastructure must keep pace with the growing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), particularly as more affordable models become increasingly accessible to Malaysians. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the government must ensure the country's EV ecosystem develops alongside technological advancements and growing EV adoption. Johari said the country could face problems if EV adoption accelerated without sufficient public infrastructure.

items.title: Five PKR MPs accuse party of abusing power over MyKhas access
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Five PKR lawmakers have criticised the party's decision to block Ampang member of parliament Rodziah Ismail's access to the MyKhas special allocation portal, describing it as an abuse of power. In a joint statement today, they said the move denied Rodziah the ability to manage the parliamentary allocation for Ampang. They also stressed that allocations channelled through MyKhas were not a gift from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to elected representatives.

items.title: No need for early GE16, unity government intact, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: There is no need for an early general election (GE16) as the unity government remains intact, says Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. "We should wait for a statement from the Dewan Rakyat speaker. "Anything involving the Dewan Rakyat, including seats in the Dewan Rakyat, requires an official announcement from the speaker.

items.title: Fahmi: PKR rejected Nurul Izzah's resignation, granted her leave instead
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The PKR Central Leadership Council rejected Nurul Izzah Anwar's request to step down as deputy president, says Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. The PKR information chief said the decision was made during a recent council meeting. He was responding to questions on whether Nurul Izzah's decision would impact PKR.

items.title: Haze worsens in Sarawak as 5 areas record unhealthy air
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions in Sarawak worsened today, with five areas recording unhealthy air quality as forest and land fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, continued to contribute to deteriorating conditions. The Environment Department said Serian recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 171 as of 8am, followed by Kuching and Samarahan at 154 each, Sri Aman (139) and Bintulu (124). "The air quality worsened today with an increase in areas recording unhealthy API levels, especially in Sarawak," it said in a statement.

items.title: Largest reservoir in US falls to record low amid prolonged drought
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: Lake Mead, the largest reservoir in the United States (US), has fallen to its lowest water level since it was first filled in 1937 amid a prolonged drought, according to data from the US Bureau of Reclamation, reported Xinhua. The lake's water elevation dropped to 317.14 metres, according to the bureau. The Colorado River flows through seven states and provides water to 40 million people, according to the bureau.

items.title: King orders thorough probe into Tabung Haji RCI report, says guilty parties must face action
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia today decreed that the investigation into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on the Tabung Haji (TH) Board be carried out exhaustively. In a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s official Facebook, His Majesty said that the move is important to ensure that all parties responsible are appropriately dealt with, as well as to ensure that the same thing does not happen again in the future. In addition, Sultan Ibrahim also said that the investigation into the matter should be carried out comprehensively, without compromising on any party found guilty.

items.title: Bersama to unveil Melaka election candidates on Aug 15, says Rafizi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) will announce its candidates for the Melaka election on Aug 15, party leader Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said. The former economy minister said preparations for the polls had entered their final stage, with the party's candidate list finalised. The next Melaka election must be held by February 2027, although Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has reportedly indicated that the polls could be held as early as September.

items.title: Fahmi: Constituency allocations at PM’s discretion, funds should go directly to people
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The special constituency allocation is at the discretion of the Prime Minister, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today, amid controversy over several PKR MPs losing access to the MyKhas portal. Fahmi said the allocation was not a personal entitlement of MPs and that the Prime Minister had the prerogative to determine how the funds were channelled for the benefit of constituents. He said the mechanism announced by Anwar would see allocations for MPs managed through the Prime Minister’s political office.

items.title: Political cooperation must not disrupt stability, says Johari
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Any political cooperation between parties must not compromise political stability, which is vital for economic development and investor confidence, says Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. He said political stability was crucial to ensuring the consistent implementation of economic policies without the disruption of frequent changes in government. Johari said investors evaluate a country's political stability before committing capital, adding that stability forms the bedrock of economic progress.

items.title: Fahmi: AI cannot replace human moderators in detecting cyberbullying, Tamil language a case in point
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Artificial intelligence (AI) cannot be left entirely in charge of moderating online content as it may fail to understand the nuances of certain languages, particularly when dealing with cyberbullying, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. He said this was particularly evident in cases involving cyberbullying within the Tamil-speaking community, where AI-based moderation could fail to properly identify harmful or abusive content. He said the two codes were intended to ensure social media platforms did not become hubs for crimes including scams, cyberbullying and other offences.

items.title: Ex-Petagas rep James Ligunjang joins Hajiji's Gagasan
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Former Petagas assemblyman Datuk James Ligunjang has officially joined Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah (Gagasan). Their membership forms were submitted to Gagasan Moyog division chief Datuk Mandela Malakun, witnessed by party Kepayan division chief Datuk Steven Jimbangan. James said joining Gagasan was a step towards strengthening the party's struggle as a component of Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS), which forms the state government.

items.title: Nurul Izzah remains party member, Anwar has full backing of govt parties, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The resignation of Nurul Izzah Anwar from her party leadership post will not affect her commitment to PKR, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. Fahmi said Nurul Izzah remained a party member and would continue to support its struggle, while stressing that component parties remained committed to supporting Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said Nurul Izzah had resigned and requested time to focus on her PhD studies, with the party’s leadership responsibilities to continue under its existing leadership structure.

items.title: [UPDATED] King: No guilty party should escape action over TH, Felda issues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, says no one guilty of any offence in issues involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) and the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) should escape action. The ruler said any investigations into the issues must be conducted comprehensively. Sultan Ibrahim was briefed on the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into TH, as well as current issues involving Felda, during an audience with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at Istana Bukit Tunku.

items.title: In death, Romaizam gives 3 others a new lease of life
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: The final wish of Romaizam Marzuan, 44, to donate her organs has given three patients a new lease of life following transplants of her kidneys and liver. Her husband, Raja Muhammad Raja Ali, 45, said her kidneys were donated to two men aged 27 and 37, while a 54-year-old man received her liver. I hope those who received her organs can lead better lives and enjoy good health for many years to come," he said when contacted.

items.title: Police corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz laid to rest laid after Sabah tragedy
items.summary: His eldest sister, 34-year-old Nurlella Rahim, said her family expressed their appreciation to the police for assisting in facilitating the arrangements to bring her brother's remains home. Nurlella said the five siblings were very close and often made video calls almost every day, including through the family WhatsApp group. "We made video calls with each other almost every day.

items.title: [UPDATED] King orders tighter airport, border security to curb drug smuggling
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has ordered the authorities to tighten security controls at all airports and entry points into the country. The ruler said this was necessary to curb drug smuggling and transnational criminal activities that threaten public safety and security. Sultan Ibrahim said security at the country's entry points must be continuously strengthened through more effective enforcement, constant monitoring and cooperation among all ministries and agencies involved.

items.title: No complaints from civil servants over political pressure, says PSD
items.summary: Public Service Department (PSD) director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the department was monitoring the issue. Last Thursday, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the government would protect civil servants from pressure arising from political tensions. Zahid said civil servants must continue discharging their responsibilities in accordance with regulations and legal channels.

items.title: Residents shocked as kidnap rescue ends in deadly shootout
items.summary: ALOR STAR: Residents of Taman Amira were left in shock after a deadly shootout occurred in their quiet neighbourhood last night, with police cordoning off the housing area for nearly four hours. "The neighbour said residents were not allowed to leave or enter because police had cordoned off the area," he said when contacted today. Ooi said another neighbour heard gunshots while taking out the rubbish and immediately ran back inside.

items.title: Police corporal killed in Sabah electrocution laid to rest as family recalls final video call
items.summary: His eldest sister, 34-year-old Nurlella Rahim, said her family expressed their appreciation to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) for assisting in facilitating the arrangements to bring her brother’s remains home. Nurlella said the five siblings were very close and often made video calls almost every day, including through the family WhatsApp group. “We made video calls with each other almost every day.

items.title: Have you seen her? Police seek help to locate missing teen Dhia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are seeking public assistance to locate a 14-year-old girl who has been missing from her home in Ampang since Aug 2. Ampang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said Dhia Zahraaxavieta Neelopher Harisman was reported missing by her parents at 8.34pm yesterday. Dhia was last seen at Sri Mayang Apartment, Pandan Indah Komersil Park, Ampang.

items.title: Authorities seize 164 servers in Selangor bitcoin mining raids
items.summary: SABAK BERNAM: Authorities seized 164 servers used for illegal Bitcoin mining following joint raids on four premises in the district yesterday. The Sabak Bernam District Council (MDSB) said the operation, conducted with Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), ran from 5pm to midnight and targeted locations in Sungai Besar and Sabak Bernam town. "Four premises were inspected in Sungai Besar and Sabak Bernam town, resulting in the seizure of 164 servers.

items.title: From his quiet home to a shooting spree at school, a Thai teenager's deadly rampage
items.summary: BANG BUA THONG, Thailand: The boy shot his grandparents dead at dawn on Friday in their two-storey house bordering rice fields on the outskirts of Bangkok. Each was killed by a single gunshot to the head, a Thai police official said. Police Colonel Thadsakorn Konthong, superintendent of Bang Bua Thong Police Station, said the boy killed his elderly relatives at around 5am.

items.title: Pink suitcase scare in Bukit Kayu Hitam ICQS ends with shampoo, lotion find
items.summary: BUKIT KAYU HITAM: A security scare unfolded at the Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex after an unattended pink suitcase was found yesterday evening. Kubang Pasu police chief Superintendent Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the suitcase was discovered at about 5.55pm and taken for scanning after no one came forward to claim it. "After the scan, Customs officers detected images suggesting suspected drugs and explosives inside the suitcase."

items.title: Police neutralise unattended luggage at Bukit Kayu Hitam ICQS complex, no explosives found
items.summary: Kubang Pasu police chief Supt Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the pink luggage was found at about 5.55 pm after no one came forward to claim it. “The luggage was then taken for scanning and Customs personnel found images indicating the possible presence of suspected drugs and explosive materials. “The luggage was opened at 11 pm, and no explosive materials were found.

items.title: Singapore to charge duo over convicted opposition politician's escape to Johor
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Two Singaporean men will be charged today for allegedly conspiring to help convicted opposition politician Lim Tean flee to Malaysia. The Singapore Police Force said preliminary investigations showed the men had arranged for Lim, a lawyer, to leave the country in circumstances intended to defeat the course of justice. The offences arose from Lim attending court hearings and submitting documents on 32 occasions between April and June 2021 without a valid practising certificate.

items.title: Trump administration to invest $3bil into minerals projects to boost US defence supply chains
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Friday the federal government would invest US$3 billion into multiple critical minerals and battery projects as part of a push to increase domestic production and boost national security and industrial policy. The OSC also extended a US$400 million conditional loan to scandium miner Sunrise Energy Metals and a US$150 million conditional loan to magnet developer Niron Magnetics. The US Export-Import Bank will lend US$58 million to Westwater Resources, Global Advanced Metals and 5E Advanced Materials, which Reuters reported earlier on Friday.

items.title: Police kill two suspects in shootout during Alor Setar kidnap rescue operation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Two suspects, believed to be foreigners, were killed in a shootout with police during an operation to rescue two kidnap victims at a house in Taman Amira, Telaga Bata, Alor Setar, Kedah, last night. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the incident occurred at about 8.40 pm when the suspects fired several shots at the Special Investigation Division (D9) team from the Bukit Aman CID. Kumar said police also found a Beretta semi-automatic pistol loaded with five rounds of ammunition, a revolver containing four rounds of ammunition and a long machete near the two suspects.

items.title: Explainer: How could New Mexico's US$567mil ruling change Meta?
items.summary: A NEW MEXICO state court ordered Meta Platforms, owner of Facebook and Instagram, to make major changes to its platforms and pay the largest sum yet in a growing wave of US. litigation over claims that social media harms young people. HOW MUCH MUST META PAY?

items.title: Education minister challenges vocational students to use drones to improve school security
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Students of Setapak Vocational College have been challenged to develop innovative ways of using drone technology to enhance security on their school campus. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the students had been given one month to study and identify the best ways to apply the technology before presenting their proposals to her. “Within a month, I want the students to present to me how drone technology can be used to help improve school security,” she said in a Facebook post yesterday.

items.title: Malaysia, Cambodia strengthen defence ties, cooperation in AI and drone technology
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Malaysia and Cambodia are committed to further strengthening bilateral ties, particularly in defence and security, while contributing to Asean’s collective resilience. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the commitment was expressed during his courtesy call on Cambodian Prime Minister Samdech Thipadei Hun Manet at the Peace Palace in Phnom Penh yesterday. He said Malaysia and Cambodia are also committed to strengthening defence cooperation in new areas, including jungle warfare training, the defence industry, artificial intelligence (AI) and drone technology.

items.title: Abang Johari urges community leaders to bridge govt, people
items.summary: SARIKEI, Aug 8 — Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg has urged community leaders and heads of ethnic groups to continue serving as a bridge between the government and the people to ensure the state’s development policies are well understood. He said a clear understanding of government policies was essential to prevent misconceptions that could undermine social harmony, investor confidence and the state’s economic growth. “Community leaders are not only grassroots leaders but also play an important role in communicating government policies so that the people understand the direction of the state’s development,” he said when speaking at a dinner with community leaders and heads of ethnic groups here last night.

items.title: OpenAI flags possible critical cybersecurity risk in upcoming model, tightens controls
items.summary: WASHINGTON: OpenAI said on Friday it cannot rule out that its upcoming AI model, Astra, has "critical" cybersecurity capabilities, prompting the startup to pause some internal development and trigger safety protocols. * Preliminary evaluations over the past several days, along with outside expert assessments, indicated Astra may be capable of performing increasingly sophisticated cyber tasks autonomously, OpenAI said. * OpenAI also clarified that Astra was not involved in the hack targeting the AI platform Hugging Face.

items.title: Razali denies joining Pejuang after quitting as Terengganu Bersatu chief
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: Former Terengganu Bersatu chief Datuk Razali Idris has denied claims that he has joined Perikatan Nasional component Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang). Razali, who announced his resignation as state chief yesterday, said he was still a Bersatu member. Commenting on reports that Telemong assemblyman Mohd Zawawi Ismail and Hulu Besut assemblyman Mohd Husaimi Hussin had resigned as Terengganu Bersatu information chief and treasurer, respectively, Razali said he had only learned about the matter through media reports.

items.title: Trump ally Abelardo de la Espriella sworn in as Colombia president
items.summary: CALI, Colombia: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella took office Friday, vowing to wage war on drug-running guerrillas and usher in a new era of close ties with the United States. De la Espriella and his Vice President Jose Manuel Restrepo cheered, embraced and performed their campaign's characteristic military salute after taking their respective oaths. De la Espriella's leftist predecessor Gustavo Petro declined to attend the ceremony.

items.title: Trump renews effort to remove US Fed Governor Lisa Cook
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump is moving forward with an attempt to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over mortgage fraud allegations, according to a White House letter seen by AFP on Friday, after the Supreme Court batted him back in June. Cook has been given 21 days from the date of the letter to respond to unproven allegations that she made false statements on mortgage applications – charges that she has denied. His move to dismiss Cook was the first such attempt by a president in the US central bank's 111-year history.

items.title: Selangor to empower local entrepreneurs to compete globally, says Amirudin
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 8 — The Selangor government remains committed to empowering local entrepreneurs to ensure they can grow sustainably and remain competitive in an evolving digital economy. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said empowering entrepreneurs remains a priority for his administration, as micro-entrepreneurs are among the key drivers of the state’s economic growth. Meanwhile, Menteri Besar Selangor (Incorporated) (MBI Selangor) group chief executive officer Datuk Saipolyazan M Yusop said MAPS 2026 was organised to recognise the perseverance, resilience and innovative spirit of entrepreneurs.

items.title: IGP hails new promotion system as boost to morale, career progression
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) described the government’s initiative to introduce a new promotion method for members of the security forces and the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) as a significant recognition and morale booster for both services. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the move, which was highly anticipated by PDRM personnel, reflected the government’s concern for those entrusted with the responsibility of safeguarding public safety and order. He expressed his deepest appreciation to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for the government’s attention towards the agenda of strengthening the career advancement of national security forces personnel.

items.title: MACC completes fourth, final day of recording former CFO’s statement in Tabung Haji probe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 8 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has completed recording the statement of a former chief financial officer (CFO) of a statutory body-owned company, as part of its probe into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the individual’s statement was taken to obtain evidence regarding allegations of abuse of power in the purchase of shares in two plantation companies valued at approximately RM370 million. The investigation focuses on alleged abuse of power in the RM370 million purchase of shares in two plantation companies, as raised in the RCI report on Lembaga Tabung Haji.

items.title: Kamil: Nurul Izzah's decision to step down won't affect Melaka polls preparations
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR: Nurul Izzah Anwar's move to step down as PKR deputy president will not derail party preparations for the Melaka election, said PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim. He said statements by party leadership and Nurul Izzah provided sufficient clarification on her departure. On Thursday, PKR granted Nurul Izzah temporary leave following her request to step down as deputy president.

items.title: #NSTviral: No running shoes, no problem: Indonesian clocks 1,946-day streak [WATCH]
items.summary: In a post yesterday marking day 1,946 of his running streak, Restu said one of the biggest benefits of running was that it helped him manage his weight without resorting to complicated diets. His choice of running gear has also become part of his appeal, with Restu frequently seen running in sandals instead of conventional running shoes. Another user, @skii.rant, praised Restu for maintaining the streak without the usual sportswear or running shoes.

items.title: Tabung Haji to study NGO proposals, says 75pc of RCI recommendations implemented
items.summary: In a statement yesterday, TH said the memorandum submitted by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on TH Himpunan Aman Solidariti reflected the public’s genuine concern in supporting the national haj institution to safeguard the interests of the Muslim community. “TH also supports the government’s firm action in taking the necessary measures based on the findings of the RCI. Earlier, the Himpunan Gerakan Islam Malaysia (HIKAM) and the Coalition of Islamic NGOs submitted a memorandum containing 10 demands related to the TH RCI report.

items.title: Two men arrested over podcast allegedly touching on religious sensitivities, say police
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 8 — Police confirmed the arrest of two local men following a report received regarding a podcast episode that allegedly touched on religious sensitivities. North Klang District Police Chief ACP Ramsay Embol said his department received the report on August 5 before the arrests of a freelance host and a businessman, aged in their 30s and 60s respectively, were carried out yesterday. “Police have received a report regarding a video clip of a podcast created by two individuals discussing the issues of secular and liberal ideologies.

items.title: Anwar: Political differences must not stand in way of Federal-state cooperation
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 8 — Differences in the political parties governing the Federal and state governments should not stand in the way of friendship and cooperation between them, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said close ties and cooperation were essential to ensure the people continued to benefit from government initiatives. “Our system of government requires close cooperation.

items.title: Houthi attacks kill 10 in Yemen as rebels target oil-rich Marib
items.summary: A 2022 truce between the Iranian-backed Houthis and the Saudi-supported Yemen government unravelled last month and at least 58 government troops were killed in rebel missile attacks on Marib province on Thursday. A Yemeni military source told AFP that the latest Houthi attacks in Marib killed eight members of government forces and wounded 12 others. The rebels said they had attacked a government military camp in Marib province.

items.title: New promotion method a morale boost for security forces, says IGP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The police have welcomed the government's move to introduce a new promotion method for personnel in the force and the Malaysian Armed Forces, describing the initiative as a significant recognition and morale boost for both services. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the move, which was highly anticipated by police personnel, reflected the government's concern for those entrusted with the responsibility of safeguarding public safety and order. He expressed his deepest appreciation to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for the government's attention towards the agenda of strengthening the career advancement of national security forces personnel.

items.title: Stay or go? DAP faces catch-22 as crucial congress vote looms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — DAP delegates will gather on August 16 for the party’s national congress, where they will face a political catch-22 that could shape its strategy heading into the next general election. Roughly 4,000 delegates are expected to vote on whether DAP leaders should remain in government posts, including the federal Cabinet, or relinquish those positions while continuing to support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in Parliament. Many voters may not distinguish between leaving the executive and continuing to support the government in Parliament.

items.title: Anwar questions RM330m gap in proposed Felda hotel sale, orders full report
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the management of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) to provide a complete report regarding the proposed sale of a hotel owned by the agency, which was allegedly at a price far lower than the original purchase price. “Felda is under my watch. “Felda settlers are struggling.

items.title: Anwar: Govt to cut red tape in military, police promotion process
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said details of the new mechanism are expected to be announced during the Ambang Merdeka celebration at Stadium Merdeka in Kuala Lumpur on August 30. He said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Public Service director-general Tan Sri Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz are currently finalising the implementation mechanism. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Dr Mohd Na’im Mokhtar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Shamsul Azri and Army Chief Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.

items.title: Malaysia and Singapore to deepen labour cooperation, boost protection for gig workers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Malaysia and Singapore will continue to strengthen cooperation in the labour sector, including enhancing the welfare and protection of gig workers, as both countries navigate an increasingly dynamic employment landscape. He said both sides exchanged views on current labour market developments and the challenges facing Malaysia and Singapore in preparing their workforce to meet the demands of the future economy. “Malaysia and Singapore are facing rapid changes in the employment landscape.

items.title: Woman hurt after SUV crashes into KKIA departure hall
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — A woman was injured after the sport utility vehicle (SUV) she was driving reportedly lost control and crashed through the glass entrance of the departure hall at Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) this afternoon. The incident, which occurred at about 4.20pm, shattered the glass doors of the departure hall and sent broken glass across the passenger walkway, causing panic among members of the public at the scene. Early indications suggest the driver may have accidentally pressed the accelerator, causing the vehicle to surge forward and crash into the terminal.

items.title: Ismail Sabri stable after successful pacemaker implantation at IJN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob’s pacemaker implantation procedure this afternoon at the National Heart Institute (IJN) was carried out successfully, his lawyer has confirmed. When contacted by Malay Mail , Ismail Sabri’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad confirmed that “the procedure went smoothly and was successful”. IJN later said Ismail Sabri had successfully undergone a leadless pacemaker implantation procedure for an abnormal heart rhythm this afternoon.

items.title: Malaysia to increase defence spending in Budget 2027, says Anwar
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 7 — The government will seek to increase defence allocation in Budget 2027 to strengthen the Malaysian Armed Forces’ (MAF) readiness and improve personnel welfare, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said greater investment was necessary to safeguard national peace, which he described as the country’s most valuable asset. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Army chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.

items.title: MACC urges ministry chiefs to protect whistleblowers as Malaysia eyes higher CPI ranking
items.summary: MACC’s National Governance Planning Division deputy director Mohd Gunawan Che Ab Aziz said the move is critical to remove civil servants’ fear of reporting misconduct and, in turn, bolster organisational integrity. He said secretaries-general and directors-general must translate the government’s commitment to amending the Whistleblower Protection Act 2010 down to the grassroots level, to ensure that the Integrity Unit in every ministry functions independently and reports directly to the MACC. Mohd Gunawan said that beyond strengthening whistleblower protection, secretaries-general and directors-general must lead comprehensive reforms in public procurement and contract systems, including full open tenders and mandatory declarations of beneficial ownership for all bidding companies.

items.title: Yayasan Tuanku Fauziah launches Women in Technology Awards 2026 to honour Malaysian innovators
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — Yayasan Tuanku Fauziah (YTF) has launched the Women in Technology Awards 2026, a national initiative to recognise outstanding Malaysian women, whose leadership, innovation and technological achievements are shaping the country’s future. Two categories will be offered — the Senior Women in Technology Award, worth RM30,000, for professionals with at least 20 years’ experience, and the Junior Women in Technology Award, worth RM15,000, for innovators aged 35 and below or with under 10 years’ experience. YTF said the awards celebrate exceptional Malaysian women whose contributions have advanced science, technology and innovation, inspiring greater participation in STEM and encouraging future generations of innovators and leaders.

items.title: Immigration Dept gears up for F1 Bahrain GP visitor surge at Sepang
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Immigration Department (JIM) will ensure that immigration procedures involving visas and related passes at the country’s entry points run smoothly during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) this October. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department would work closely with the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) to ensure clearance procedures at the country's entry points are carried out efficiently while complying with all security requirements. “We must provide the best possible service to ensure the smooth organisation of the Formula 1 event.

items.title: Immigration busts ‘flying passport’ syndicate, three arrested in Johor
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM) has dismantled a “flying passport” syndicate with the arrest of three suspects at the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB) in Gelang Patah, Johor, yesterday, said Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban. He said the operation, which began at 10am, involved a team of officers and personnel from the Putrajaya Immigration headquarters Intelligence and Special Operations Division and Johor JIM. He said the team also seized mobile phones, keys to a premise, jewellery, Immigration security stamps and RM20,000 in cash.

items.title: Indonesian maid jailed four years for neglect that led to toddler’s drowning in Sentul pool
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — An Indonesian domestic helper was sentenced to four years’ jail by the Sessions Court here today after she pleaded guilty to neglecting a boy, resulting in his death by drowning in an adult swimming pool last month. According to the charge, Wahyuni, as a person responsible for the care of a two-year-three-month-old boy, neglected the child, resulting in his death. According to the facts of the case, the victim’s mother had instructed the accused, who was employed as her domestic helper, to take the victim and his five-year-old brother to the swimming pool at their residential complex on the day of the incident.

items.title: Remains of three policemen killed in Beaufort electrocution incident sent home after post-mortem
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — The remains of three police officers who died believed to be from electrocution outside the Weston Police Station, Beaufort, yesterday afternoon were brought out from the Forensic Department of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital (HQE) at 2:55 pm today to be sent back to their respective hometowns. The remains of Corporal Chiu Teck Siong will be taken to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Air Operations Force (PGU) Airfield here before being flown to Sarawak. Meanwhile, Beaufort District Police Chief Supt Champin Piuh expressed his appreciation to Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun, members of the Sabah Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK), and HQE for their extensive assistance in facilitating the management of the remains.

items.title: Bersatu sec‑gen Azmin Ali says party remains legitimate Perikatan component despite PAS claim
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali today hit back at PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s assertion that the party’s membership in Perikatan Nasional (PN) had automatically lapsed, describing the claim as unconstitutional. He stressed that Bersatu’s position could only be decided by the PN presidential council under Clause 7A of the coalition’s constitution. Therefore, Bersatu remains a legitimate component party of Perikatan Nasional,” Azmin said.
